founding_narrative.story_arc: When dialogue matters, the conditions must hold — a protected room, a structured process, and an outcome people can verify without exposing who was in the room.
founding_narrative.through_line: Ordinary tools fail sensitive dialogue. SquadRidge holds one clear line between the conversation and the record.

founder_mission.quote: Some of us learned early that blame travels faster than truth, and that the wrong room can end a conversation before it starts. SquadRidge is the infrastructure we wished existed: a protected space to speak, a structured path forward, and a record people can verify without exposing who was in the room.
founder_mission.note: Values-forward founding statement. Belief-framed, not a customer testimonial. Deeper personal north star lives in docs/founding/north-star.md for contributors only.

belief_quote_landing.quote: We kept seeing sensitive conversations stall the moment someone feared a leak — and fall apart when there was no credible way to show what had been agreed. We built SquadRidge to hold one clear line between the dialogue and the record, so parties can speak freely and still stand behind what they release.

decision_tests: Uniqueness: does this strengthen room/record separation — or blur it?
Versatility: does this help another real context without becoming a generic chat app?
Security: can we state the privacy property honestly in threat-model.md?
Adaptability: does the facilitator stay in control of judgment and release?
Real impact: does this help produce a verifiable outcome for an actual dispute or institution?
Founding purpose: does this protect vulnerable people in the room — not expose them?
tone_rules: Calm, precise, trust-building — never alarmist or militarized
Honest about limits — never claim E2E or legal protection without engineering sign-off
Facilitator authority — automate workflow, never judgment or release
No fabricated customer testimonials during pilot stage

Facilitator-controlled session lifecycle: Configure → Verify → Facilitate → Release
Role-based access with private identity verification (participants verified, never disclosed publicly)
Facilitator-approved outcomes only — no raw session data is ever published
Verification anchor on every released record (tamper-evident, independently checkable)

is_not: NOT a video or audio call platform — no calls, now or in the current product vision
NOT a general-purpose messaging app — purpose-built for high-stakes facilitated dialogue
NOT a recording platform — session dialogue is not published as a transcript; no audio or video is captured

unbreakable_promises: Without exposing who said what — the public record never reveals participant identities or attributions

no_video_decision.statement: SquadRidge is a facilitator-led messaging room only. It does not build, host, or integrate with video or audio calls.
no_video_decision.rationale: Calls expose participant identity (faces, voices, surroundings), introduce recording risks, and blur the line between the protected room and the released record. The product is structured written dialogue under facilitator control — not a call surface with a record bolted on.
no_video_decision.framing: Frame as 'facilitator-led messaging room' — the entire protected dialogue happens in SquadRidge. Never suggest external call tools or 'use video elsewhere'.
no_video_decision.out_of_scope: Video calls, audio calls, call integrations, and audio-only sessions must NOT be referenced on any current page.

automation_architecture.communication_principle: Frame automation as 'the system handles the workflow so the facilitator can focus on the dialogue.' Never frame it as removing human control — it removes manual overhead while preserving human authority at every decision point.

must_automate.name: Verification anchor generation
must_automate.trigger: Facilitator clicks Release (after all approvals captured).
must_automate.action: System generates the integrity hash, creates the anchor, publishes to the ledger, and makes it independently verifiable — one click.
must_automate.human_role: Facilitator makes the deliberate Release decision; the hash/publish is fully automated.

must_automate.name: Participant identity verification flow
must_automate.action: System sends verification links, tracks status (pending/verified/declined), and grants room access only after verification completes. Facilitator sees a green/red status dashboard per participant.
must_automate.human_role: Facilitator makes the identity judgment call; the system runs the flow and status tracking.

must_automate.name: Room access provisioning
must_automate.trigger: Participant verified; or session ends / facilitator closes room.
must_automate.action: Role-based permissions granted automatically on verification; access revoked automatically on close. No manual access management.

must_automate.name: Record redaction enforcement
must_automate.trigger: Facilitator assembles the outcome for release.
must_automate.action: System architecturally prevents unapproved content from reaching the release stage. Only content the facilitator explicitly includes can enter the record; everything else stays in the room and is never copyable into the record.
must_automate.human_role: Facilitator chooses what to include; the constraint is enforced by design.

must_automate.name: Ledger publishing
must_automate.action: Record appears automatically on the public ledger with anchor, metadata, and outcome text. No manual publishing step.

must_automate.name: Session lifecycle state machine
must_automate.trigger: Session progresses through Configure → Verify → Facilitate → Release.
must_automate.action: State-machine-driven: cannot facilitate before required participants verify; cannot release before facilitation is complete. Prevents skipping steps.
must_automate.human_role: Facilitator advances stages deliberately; the machine prevents invalid transitions.

should_automate.name: Notification system
should_automate.action: Automated notifications at key points: invitation to verify, room open, new prompt posted, approval requested, record released. Fully wired, not just UI.

should_automate.name: Approval capture workflow
should_automate.action: On outcome draft, system sends approval requests to all verified participants, tracks approved/pending/declined, and only allows release once all approvals are captured. No manual email threads.

should_automate.name: Session archival and room closure
should_automate.action: After release, room archives automatically (content preserved but read-only; access revoked for non-facilitators). No manual cleanup.

should_automate.name: Audit trail logging
should_automate.action: Every action (verification, room entry, prompt posted, approval given, record released) is logged automatically to an internal audit trail. Supports the tamper-evidence promise.

must_not_automate.name: Outcome drafting
must_not_automate.reason: Facilitator must write/co-write what becomes public. AI-assisted suggestions may help in the future, but final text must be human-authored and human-approved.

must_not_automate.name: Verification of participant identity (judgment)
must_not_automate.reason: System handles the flow, but the facilitator makes the judgment about who is who. Never auto-verify on email alone.

must_not_automate.name: Release decision
must_not_automate.reason: Facilitator must explicitly click Release. Never automatic, timed, or condition-triggered.

must_not_automate.name: Redaction decisions
must_not_automate.reason: Facilitator chooses what goes into the outcome. System may flag potentially sensitive content for review, but humans decide.

ridge_protocol.tagline: A controlled crossing — structured written rounds, not a chat flood.
ridge_protocol.communication_principle: The Ridge Protocol is SquadRidge's signature facilitation mode: parties cross the ridge one round at a time, under facilitator gatekeeping. Frame as process infrastructure for high-stakes dialogue — never as surveillance or auto-moderation.

stages.label: Configure
stages.summary: Set the session up before anyone is invited.
sub_steps: Facilitator sets session title, ground rules, and participant eligibility criteria.

stages.label: Verify
stages.summary: Confirm who belongs in the room — privately.

System automatically sends verification requests and tracks status (pending / verified / declined).
Each participant verifies privately; identity data is visible only to the facilitator.

stages.label: Facilitate
stages.summary: Run the dialogue as structured, written exchange.
sub_steps: The room opens as a structured, text-based dialogue environment — not a video call.
The facilitator poses prompts or opens rounds; parties respond in writing.
The conversation is organized into protected threads.

stages.label: Release

intro.heading: Who SquadRidge is built for
intro.body: SquadRidge is not a general-purpose platform, and it is not a video tool. It was purpose-built for facilitator-led, text-based dialogue where the room must stay private and the outcome must be credible. Every scenario below follows the same shape: structured written dialogue in the room, an approved and verifiable record out.

cases.heading: Community land-use mediation
cases.scenario: A regional mediation center facilitates dialogue between community groups and local government over watershed land use.
cases.in_the_room: Structured rounds where each party submits its position in writing; the facilitator organizes responses; parties respond to each other's positions. No faces, voices, or transcripts.
cases.out_as_record: A Joint Statement of Principles — 12 verified participants, anchor SQR-2024-0147 — published to the ledger.
cases.why_squadridge: Community members can participate without fear of public exposure; government gets a verifiable record; the process is transparent without being a transcript.

cases.heading: Sensitive internal deliberation
cases.scenario: A peacebuilding NGO's field team and headquarters deliberate on whether to publicly endorse a controversial peace framework.
cases.in_the_room: Structured dialogue where field staff can voice concerns without their names attached to positions; leadership hears all perspectives.
cases.out_as_record: A decision memo with rationale. The funder receives a verifiable record that a deliberation occurred and a decision was reached.
cases.why_squadridge: Staff are never put at risk by their own participation; the funder gets evidence of process without a transcript that could be weaponized.

cases.heading: Cross-border Track II dialogue
cases.scenario: Civil society groups from conflicting parties convene to explore confidence-building measures.
cases.in_the_room: The facilitator structures written rounds where each side submits positions, responds to the other, and negotiates terms — all in the protected messaging room.
cases.out_as_record: A joint communiqué — verified participants, anchor — shareable with international mediators and funders.
cases.why_squadridge: Parties speak freely knowing nothing is recorded; the communiqué is verifiable without revealing who said what.

cases.heading: Post-agreement implementation monitoring
cases.scenario: Parties to a peace agreement report on implementation progress; the facilitator releases periodic verified status updates.
cases.in_the_room: Each party submits progress reports in a structured format; the facilitator reviews and organizes them into a protected thread.
cases.out_as_record: A verified status update with an anchor, published to the ledger at agreed intervals.
cases.why_squadridge: Creates a tamper-evident record of implementation without exposing which party reported what.

security.layout: Dense, structured, technical detail with clear hierarchy. Trust-building through transparency. Should withstand a security professional's scrutiny.

intro.heading: Verified, not exposed.
intro.body: Security in SquadRidge comes from architecture, not policy language alone. Raw session content is not published. Only facilitator-approved outcomes are released, each carrying a verification anchor that can be checked independently.

architecture_separation.heading: Two layers, two responsibilities.
architecture_separation.body: The room and the record are two different objects. Inside the room: private, verified, facilitator-controlled. Released as record: approved, verifiable, deliberately narrow.

identity_model.heading: Directional anonymity: verified, but not disclosed.
identity_model.body: Participants are verified privately by the facilitator before entering the room. Identity is confirmed but never appears in the released record — no names, attributions, or identifying details. Verification data is visible only to the facilitator; other participants see only the display name and role assigned during onboarding.

data_handling.stored: Session text in the protected room — facilitator prompts and participant responses in structured format.
data_handling.never_stored: No video, no audio, no recordings, and no transcripts beyond the structured text participants contribute.
data_handling.published: The facilitator-approved outcome text only, with its verification anchor.
data_handling.explicit_statement: SquadRidge does not capture, store, or transmit video or audio.

verification_anchor.heading: What the anchor is — and isn't.
verification_anchor.body: A verification anchor is a cryptographic hash of the released record, generated automatically at the moment of release. Anyone with the record can recompute the anchor and confirm the record has not been altered since — no account required.
proves: The record has not been altered since release.
The record was issued through SquadRidge (not fabricated externally).
The organisation, date, and any included metadata are the ones on file.
does_not_prove: What was said inside the room — the private session is not encoded in the anchor.
Who each participant is — identity does not appear on the released record.
That any external party endorses the outcome — endorsement is out of scope.

room_access.heading: Role-based access, revoked on close.
room_access.body: Access to any protected area requires an active invitation tied to a session or an approved organisational role. Permissions are granted automatically on verification and revoked automatically when the session closes — no residual access, no manual access management.

audit_trail.heading: Every action, logged automatically.
audit_trail.body: Verification, room entry, prompt posted, approval given, and record released are each written to an internal audit trail automatically. This append-only log underpins the tamper-evidence promise.

safeguards.heading: Verified access only
safeguards.body: Every participant passes a facilitator-configured verification process before entering a room.

safeguards.heading: Controlled release
safeguards.body: No outcome is published without every designated approver signing off. The platform cannot unilaterally release anything.

safeguards.heading: Text-based room only
safeguards.body: The room is a facilitator-led messaging environment by design. SquadRidge does not record, store, or transmit audio or video, and does not integrate with external call tools.

safeguards.heading: Minimal retention
safeguards.body: Only the data required to facilitate the session and produce the record is retained. Room dialogue does not persist past session archival.

safeguards.heading: Participant identity protection
safeguards.body: Personal contact information is not shared between participants; verification data never surfaces to others in the room or on the record.

safeguards.heading: Auditable release chain
safeguards.body: Every approval and release action is logged; the verification anchor lets outside parties confirm the record has not been altered since.

what_we_do_not_claim: We do not claim end-to-end encryption of session content at this time. Content transits over TLS and is encrypted at rest, but it is not operator-proof end-to-end encryption; room-level E2EE is on the development roadmap.
We do not guarantee anonymity. We guarantee identity protection within the session context and controlled release of outcomes.
We do not provide legal protection. SquadRidge is a process platform, not a legal instrument.
We are not a whistleblower platform. If your threat model includes state-level adversaries, assess accordingly.

about.heading: Why we built SquadRidge
narrative: Most dialogue fails not because people are unwilling to talk, but because the conditions are wrong. The room is unsafe. The process has no structure. The outcome is unverifiable. And the technology — if used at all — was built for something else entirely.

SquadRidge was built to address a specific gap: there was no serious, purpose-built platform for facilitator-led, high-stakes dialogue that combined participant protection, process control, and a credible path to a public outcome record.

We made a deliberate architectural choice: SquadRidge is a facilitator-led messaging room only. There are no video calls, audio sessions, or parallel chat surfaces — the entire protected dialogue happens in structured written rounds under facilitator control. That preserves a clear line between the private room and the released record.

SquadRidge is not a collaboration tool. It is structured facilitation infrastructure. The session room is private. The approved outcome can be public. And every step between those two states is controlled by the facilitator, not the platform.

We are in an early access phase — a private pilot, now inviting mediators and peacebuilding teams. We work closely with pilot partners to make sure the platform is fit for purpose before broader release.

founder_mission.quote: We kept seeing sensitive conversations stall the moment someone feared a leak — and fall apart when there was no credible way to show what had been agreed. We built SquadRidge to hold one clear line between the dialogue and the record, so parties can speak freely and still stand behind what they release.
founder_mission.note: Belief-framed team statement, not a named-persona quote. If attributing to a real named founder later, use their real name.

principles: The room is private. Always. The outcome is public only if approved.
Facilitators are in control of the session lifecycle, not the platform.
Participants must be eligible. Verification is not optional for high-stakes sessions.
Public records must be credible. We do not publish unverified or unapproved content.
We are honest about what the platform does and does not guarantee.

faq.layout: Accordion / Q&A list, scannable. Self-service answers.

questions.q: Who can see what is said in a room?
questions.a: Only verified participants and the facilitator. The room content — every prompt, every response — stays in the room. No transcript is ever generated, and nothing said in the room can appear in the released record unless the facilitator explicitly includes it in the approved outcome.

A tamper-evident integrity marker attached to every released record. It's generated automatically at the moment of release and can be checked independently by anyone — without an account, without contacting SquadRidge. If even a character of the record is altered after release, the anchor will not verify.

Participants are verified privately by the facilitator before they enter the room. Their identity is confirmed but never appears in the released record — no names, no attributions, no identifying details. The public record shows only the number of verified participants and the approved outcome.

Not yet — and we won't say otherwise. Session data is encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest, but this is not operator-proof end-to-end encryption today: SquadRidge's infrastructure can technically access room content. Room-level end-to-end encryption, so that even our infrastructure cannot read dialogue text, is on our roadmap. Regardless of encryption model, room content is never published — only the facilitator-approved outcome is released.
questions.honesty_note: This is the real, non-placeholder answer, grounded in the current implementation (TLS + encryption at rest; E2EE on roadmap). Do not upgrade this claim to 'end-to-end encrypted' until the implementation actually supports it.

questions.q: How long does it take to set up a session?
questions.a: A facilitator can configure a room in minutes — set the ground rules, invite participants, and the system handles verification automatically. Most rooms are ready to open within the same day, once all participants complete their private verification.

questions.q: Does SquadRidge support video or audio calls?
questions.a: No. SquadRidge is a facilitator-led messaging room only — structured written dialogue under facilitator control. There are no video calls, audio sessions, or call integrations. Only the facilitator-approved outcome is released, with a verification anchor.

questions.q: Can SquadRidge be used for arbitration or legal mediation?
questions.a: SquadRidge is designed for facilitated dialogue and joint outcome statements, not for binding arbitration. For formal legal mediation, consult your jurisdiction's requirements.

questions.q: What happens to room data after a record is released?
questions.a: The room is archived — content is preserved in a read-only state accessible only to the facilitator. Participant access is revoked. The room content is never published and can never become part of the public record.

SquadRidge is currently in private pilot. We are pursuing grant funding from peacetech and conflict-resolution funders, not venture capital, to keep our mission and incentives aligned with the mediation community.
